arxiv-2103-11875.title: Effective discreteness radius of stabilisers for stationary actions
arxiv-2103-11875.creator: T. Gelander and A. Levit and G.A. Margulis
arxiv-2103-11875.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by T. Gelander and A. Levit and G.A. Margulis. We prove an effective variant of the Kazhdan–Margulis theorem generalized to stationary actions of semisimple groups over local fields: the probability that the stabilizer of a random point admits a non-trivial intersection with a small r r -neighborhood of the identity is at most β ​ r δ \beta r^{\delta} for some explicit constants β , δ > 0 \beta,\delta>0 depending only the group. This is a consequence of a key convolution inequality.

arxiv-2105-04945.creator: Steffen Bochenek, Cathy E. McNamee, Michael Kappl, Hans-Juergen Butt, Walter Richtering

Richtering, PCCP , 2021, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/D1CP01703A. Responsive poly- N -isopropylacrylamide-based microgels are commonly used as model colloids with soft repulsive interactions.

arxiv-2107-10560.title: The K ¯ ​ N {\bar{K}}N interaction in higher partial waves
arxiv-2107-10560.creator: Albert Feijoo, Daniel Gazda, Volodymyr Magas, Àngels Ramos
arxiv-2107-10560.description: Abstract We present a chiral K ¯ ​ N {\bar{K}}N interaction model that has been developed and optimized in order to account for the experimental data of inelastic K ¯ ​ N {\bar{K}}N reaction channels that open at higher energies.

arxiv-2303-00981.title: Differentiable Trajectory Generation for Car-like Robots with Interpolating Radial Basis Function Networks
arxiv-2303-00981.creator: Hongrui Zheng, Rahul Mangharam
arxiv-2303-00981.description: Abstract The design of Autonomous Vehicle software has largely followed the Sense-Plan-Act model. Traditional modular AV stacks develop perception, planning, and control software separately with little integration when optimizing for different objectives. On the other hand, end-to-end methods usually lack the principle provided by model-based white-box planning and control strategies.

arxiv-2405-18185.title: Revisiting the strain-induced softening behaviour in hydrogels
arxiv-2405-18185.creator: L. K. R. Duarte, L. G. Rizzi
arxiv-2405-18185.description: Abstract Usually, the strain-induced softening behaviour observed in the differential modulus K ⁡ ( T , γ ) K(T,\gamma) of hydrogels has been attributed to the breakage of internal structures of the network, such as the cross-links that bind together the polymer chains.

arxiv-2408-15194.title: Halo Mass Functions at High Redshift
arxiv-2408-15194.creator: Hannah O’Brennan 1,∗, John A. Regan 1, Chris Power 2,3, Saoirse Ward 1, John Brennan 1, Joe McCaffrey 1
arxiv-2408-15194.description: Abstract Recent JWST observations of very early galaxies, at z ≳ 10 \rm{z\gtrsim 10} , have led to claims that tension exists between the sizes and luminosities of high-redshift galaxies and what is predicted by standard Λ \Lambda CDM models.

arxiv-2504-05565.title: Cross-functional transferability in universal machine learning interatomic potentials
arxiv-2504-05565.creator: Xu Huang, Bowen Deng, Peichen Zhong, Aaron D. Kaplan, Kristin A. Persson, Gerbrand Ceder
arxiv-2504-05565.description: Abstract The rapid development of universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) has demonstrated the possibility for generalizable learning of the universal potential energy surface. In principle, the accuracy of uMLIPs can be further improved by bridging the model from lower-fidelity datasets to high-fidelity ones. In this work, we analyze the challenge of this transfer learning problem within the CHGNet framework.

arxiv-2508-08768.title: Impact of Resonance, Raman, and Thomson Scattering on Hydrogen Line Formation in Little Red Dots 2026 Impact of Resonance, Raman, and Thomson Scattering on Hydrogen Line Formation in Little Red Dots – C
arxiv-2508-08768.creator: Seok-Jun Chang, Max Gronke, Jorryt Matthee, Charlotte Mason
arxiv-2508-08768.description: Abstract Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact sources at z > 5 z>5 discovered through JWST spectroscopy. Their spectra exhibit broad Balmer emission lines ( ≳ 1000 ​ km ​ s − 1 \gtrsim 1000\rm~km~s^{-1} ), alongside absorption features and a pronounced Balmer break – evidence for a dense, neutral hydrogen medium with the n = 2 n=2 state.

pmc-10648437.title: Characterisation of Aberrant Metabolic Pathways in Hepatoblastoma Using Liquid Chromatography and Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)
pmc-10648437.creator: Alison Whitby, Pardeep Pabla, Bhoomi Shastri, Laudina Amugi, Álvaro Del Río-Álvarez, Dong-Hyun Kim, Laura Royo, Carolina Armengol, Madhumita Dandapani
pmc-10648437.description: Simple SummaryHepatoblastoma is a rare childhood liver cancer with poor outcomes for high-risk patients. Better treatments and better ways of identifying patients who respond poorly to treatment are needed. This paper uses new methods for identifying chemicals or metabolites produced in the tumour.

pmc-10717218.title: PAS domain containing regulator SLCG_7083 involved in morphological development and glucose utilization in Streptomyces lincolnensis
pmc-10717218.creator: Chun-Yan Lin, Yixian Ru, Yanchao Jin, Qi Lin, Guang-Rong Zhao
pmc-10717218.description: BackgroundStreptomyces lincolnensis is well known for producing the clinically important antimicrobial agent lincomycin. The synthetic and regulatory mechanisms on lincomycin biosynthesis have been deeply explored in recent years. However, the regulation involved in primary metabolism have not been fully addressed.ResultsSLCG_7083 protein contains a Per-Arnt-Sim (PAS) domain at the N-terminus, whose homologous proteins are highly distributed in Streptomyces.

pmc-11356036.title: Planar Micro-Supercapacitors with High Power Density Screen-Printed by Aqueous Graphene Conductive Ink
pmc-11356036.creator: Youchang Wang, Xiaojing Zhang, Yuwei Zhu, Xiaolu Li, Zhigang Shen
pmc-11356036.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple and scalable production of micro-supercapacitors (MSCs) is crucial to address the energy requirements of miniature electronics. Although significant advancements have been achieved in fabricating MSCs through solution-based printing techniques, the realization of high-performance MSCs remains a challenge. In this paper, graphene-based MSCs with a high power density were prepared through screen printing of aqueous conductive inks with appropriate rheological properties.

pmc-11357664.title: Sensors Based on Molecularly Imprinted Polymers in the Field of Cancer Biomarker Detection: A Review
pmc-11357664.creator: Camila Quezada, S. Shiva Samhitha, Alexis Salas, Adrián Ges, Luis F. Barraza, María Carmen Blanco-López, Francisco Solís-Pomar, Eduardo Pérez-Tijerina, Carlos Medina, Manuel Meléndrez
pmc-11357664.description: Biomarkers play a pivotal role in the screening, diagnosis, prevention, and post-treatment follow-up of various malignant tumors. In certain instances, identifying these markers necessitates prior treatment due to the complex nature of the tumor microenvironment. Consequently, advancing techniques that exhibit selectivity, specificity, and enable streamlined analysis hold significant importance.

pmc-11465592.title: Dense Collagen I as a Biomimetic Material to Track Matrix Remodelling in Renal Carcinomas
pmc-11465592.creator: Anuja Upadhyay, Deniz Bakkalci, Auxtine Micalet, Matt Butler, Marianne Bergin, Emad Moeendarbary, Marilena Loizidou, Umber Cheema
pmc-11465592.description: Aims: Renal tissue is a dynamic biophysical microenvironment, regulating healthy function and influencing tumor development. Matrix remodelling is an iterative process and aberrant tissue repair is prominent in kidney fibrosis and cancer. Biomimetic 3D models recapitulating the collagen composition and mechanical fidelity of native renal tissue were developed to investigate cell–matrix interactions in renal carcinomas.

pmc-11477986.title: Foraging bee species differentially prioritize quantity and quality of floral rewards
pmc-11477986.creator: Jaya Sravanthi Mokkapati, Michael Hill, Natalie K Boyle, Pierre Ouvrard, Adrien Sicard, Christina M Grozinger
pmc-11477986.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Pollinator–plant interactions represent a core mutualism that underpins biodiversity in terrestrial ecosystems, and the loss of flowering plants is a major driver of pollinator declines. Bee attraction to flowers is mediated by both quantity of resources (the number of available flowers for exploration) and quality of resources (pollen nutritional value), but whether and how bees prioritize these factors is not well understood. Here, we leveraged a unique plant system to investigate the floral factors influencing bee foraging decisions.

pmc-11533174.title: Highly Conductive Paths in Diamond and their Application in High Pressure Measurements
pmc-11533174.creator: Mateusz Gramala, Andrzej Sikora, Aleksandra Chudzyńska, Łukasz Gelczuk, Filip Dybała, Paweł Modrzyński, Robert Kudrawiec
pmc-11533174.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Diamonds possess exceptional properties such as high mechanical strength, thermal conductivity, and electrical resistance, making them suitable for various applications, including high-power electronics and optoelectronics. However, fabricating conductive structures in diamond remains a significant technological challenge. In this publication, we present a controlled process for fabricating precise amorphous conductive paths in a monocrystalline diamond using a focused ion beam (FIB) technique. The resistivity and thickness of the fabricated structures were determined, and their morphology was carefully characterized.

pmc-11633702.title: Bilateral pulvinar responsive neurostimulation for bilateral multifocal posteriorly dominant drug resistant epilepsy
pmc-11633702.creator: Richard Wang, Ariel Sacknovitz, Sima Vazquez, Jose Dominguez, Patty McGoldrick, Steven Wolf, Vishad Sukul, Carrie Muh, Sanjay E. Patra, David E. Burdette
pmc-11633702.description: ObjectiveTo describe four cases of Responsive Neurostimulation (RNS) in the bilateral pulvinar nuclei (PUL) in individuals with drug resistant epilepsy (DRE). This will show that due to widespread PUL connectivity, bilateral PUL RNS may be an option for some individuals with bilateral multifocal epilepsy.MethodsThis study comprises two centers' experience with bilateral PUL RNS for DRE.

pmc-12413550.title: Differential cell survival outcomes in response to diverse amino acid stress
pmc-12413550.creator: Marion Russier, Alessandra Fiore, Ana Bici, Annette Groß, Maria Tanzer, Assa Yeroslaviz, Matthias Mann, Peter J Murray
pmc-12413550.description: ES cells implement specialized survival strategies in response to different AA limitations, highlighting their ability to reprogram cellular biochemistry under nutrient stress. Introduction Cells continuously monitor amino acid (AA) availability to regulate metabolism, translation, and growth (Morris & Rogers, 1978; Zhu & Thompson, 2019; Gu et al, 2022).

pmc-12613839.title: Reproducible Human Neural Circuits Printed with Single-Cell Precision Reveal the Functional Roles of Ephaptic Coupling
pmc-12613839.creator: Johannes Striebel, Rouhollah Habibey, Daniel Wendland, Helge Gehring, Elizaveta Podoliak, Julia S. Pawlick, Kritika Sharma, Alex H. M. Ng, Wolfram Pernice, Volker Busskamp
pmc-12613839.description: Although in vitro neuronal models are accessible and versatile systems for functional electrophysiological studies, the spontaneous and random formation of neural circuits often compromises the structural control and reproducibility. Here, we introduce a robust method for engineering human neuronal networks in vitro with single-cell precision and reproducibility.

pmc-13099799.title: Th17/treg balance in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: the role of microbial, and genetic regulators in disease modulation
pmc-13099799.creator: Anna Giudice, Carolina Brescia, Domenico Morano, Giuseppe Viglietto, Francesco Luzza, Rosario Amato, Rocco Spagnuolo
pmc-13099799.description: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) is a chronic condition characterized by persistent mucosal inflammation driven by complex interactions among the gut microbiome, host immune genetics, and cellular metabolism. Emerging evidence highlights the central role of the Th17/Treg cell balance in maintaining intestinal immune tolerance, which is tightly regulated by microbe-derived metabolites and host metabolic pathways.

pmc-13144808.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A2434 PREDICTING FUTILITY IN PATIENTS AGED ≥80 YEARS UNDERGOING MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY: NOVEL PROGNOSTIC SCORES FOR STANDARD AND EXTENDED TIME WINDOWS
pmc-13144808.creator: Giovanni Maria D'amico, Maria Rosaria Bagnato, Leonardo Bruno, Chiara De Santis, Marina Piras, Lucia Petrangeli, Alfredo Paolo Mascolo, Giordano Lacidogna, Federico Marrama, Ilaria Maestrini, Marina Diomedi
pmc-13144808.description: Background and aimsAlthough mechanical thrombectomy significantly improved outcomes for large vessel occlusion stroke, patients aged ≥80 years remain underrepresented in randomized trials, creating uncertainty in real-world decision-making. We aimed to identify key prognostic predictors in this specific population and develop practical risk scores to guide acute management eligibility.

pmc-13319884.title: Evaluation of Parameters Determining the Pull-Out Strength of Poly(L-Lactide-Co-ε-Caprolactone) Barbed Suspension Threads: A Comparative ex vivo Study

pmc-13360879.title: Association between posterior thigh tightness and lifetime low back pain in young basketball players: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13360879.creator: Kazuyuki Watanabe, Kenichi Otoshi, Kiyomi Tsuda, Tatsuru Sonobe, Yoichi Kaneuchi, Takuya Kameda, Hiroshi Kobayashi, Kinshi Kato, Michiyuki Hakozaki, Takuya Nikaido, Yoshihiro Matsumoto
pmc-13360879.description: BackgroundLow back pain (LBP) is common in young athletes and may restrict participation in basketball. Evidence regarding the association between lower extremity tightness and LBP in adolescent basketball players remains limited. This study aimed to examine whether anterior (quadriceps) and posterior (hamstring) thigh tightness were associated with LBP in elementary and middle school players.

pmc-13364314.title: Ultra-Processed Foods Controversy: Myths, Realities, and Policy Implications
pmc-13364314.creator: Antonis Zampelas
pmc-13364314.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) have recently been associated with an increased risk of chronic diseases. However, this association remains controversial. The present commentary aims to clarify some of these controversies by summarizing the hypotheses linking UPFs to chronic diseases and critically examining the evidence regarding specific components of UPFs—such as saturated fat, added sugars, salt, and food additives—and their relationships with disease risk.
